titulo: Where the gates go: stop before what matters
lead: A flow is a task in several phases, with state saved in each one. The gate is the phase that ends and stops: the bot shows what it did and waits for you. Approving, correcting, or rejecting is the moment you manage instead of doing the work.
objetivo: put the gate in the right place in a flow and decide between approving, rejecting with a correction, or canceling.
hero_alt: Thin metal gate ajar in a dark hallway, outlined by neutral light.

aprende.t: Skill × flow: when it's worth saving state
How the gate stops and what it shows
Approve, reject with a correction, redo, or cancel

secoes.sub: The domain flow that runs in production in inemaccbot.

nos.detalhe: The command creates a numbered flow (A#9) and a list of phases. Each phase has its own state; /status shows phase by phase and audience by audience.
The agent writes a text for each audience (young people, women…). It's work you don't want to throw away if a later phase fails: that's why it's a flow, not a skill.

itens.t: shows the texts in the chat

nos.detalhe: The phase ends, the bot sends to the chat what it declared to show, and STOPS. You read, correct, and record the avatars. Only with /pronto (or /aprovar, /ok) does the flow continue.

After the gate come the expensive phases or the ones with consequences: downloading the avatar video, building the reel, and delivering it to the channel. If one fails, /refazer resumes from it, without redoing the texts.

secoes.legenda: Click each block. The gate goes after the work you need to read and before what costs money or goes out to the world.

rolagem_fim.titulo: The rule for where the gate goes
rolagem_fim.texto: After what needs your eyes, before what's expensive or public. A gate at the start has nothing to show; a gate at the end comes too late.

secoes.sub: Run the flow, read the text that stopped at the gate, and decide.
secoes.rascunho: Durable queue: your agent works all night. We guarantee 100% accuracy on every task.
secoes.corrigido: Durable queue: your agent works all night, and in the morning you check what went right and what failed.

msg.inicio: Flow A#9 created. Click "Run the flow".
msg.portao: The Texts phase finished and the flow STOPPED at the gate. Read the text below before you decide.
msg.reprovado: You rejected it with the correction "no 100% promise". The Texts phase reopened and delivered the new version. It stopped at the gate again.
msg.aprovado_ruim: Approved without fixing: the text with the false promise moved on to the video and was published. This is what the gate was for.
msg.aprovado_bom: Approved after the correction: the flow moved on to the video and published the right text.
msg.sem_portao: With | sem-portao the flow ran all the way through without waiting for you. The text reached the chat, but only after it was published.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative simulation in the browser: nothing is generated or published. The error in the text is on purpose.

secoes.sub: Each command does something different. Mixing them up costs you work.

texto: /pronto A#9 opens the gate. /aprovar, /aprovado and /ok are synonyms, and A#9, a9 and A9 are the same reference.
Without a reference, /pronto releases the flow when only one is waiting; with several, it lists which ones.

When the flow declares replies at the gate, you can answer with more than "yes": a single word, like reprova, followed by what to fix. The bot runs the domain command and the phase REOPENS with the new material.
It's the "redo it and show me until I approve". Each flow declares the replies it accepts; /ajuda <fluxo> shows which ones.
/refazer A#9 [audience] picks up from the phase that FAILED, without redoing the earlier ones.
It doesn't work for a phase stopped at the gate: that phase didn't fail, it is waiting for you. For that one, the way out is to approve or reject with a correction.
/cancelar A#9 stops the whole flow and removes it from /status. It's the last resort: to change one text, you lose all the phases.
To delete the flow's files for good, use /limpar A#9, which only shows what would go until you write confirmar.

secoes.sub: Rehearse with | sombra before spending anything.

blocos.conteudo:
/promoavatar Não comece aprendendo ferramentas | sombra
# shows phase × audience × queue and does NOT enqueue anything

/promoavatar Não comece aprendendo ferramentas --alvo=jovens
/status
/status A#9

/pronto A#9           # approves and continues
/refazer A#9 jovens   # picks up from the phase that failed
/cancelar A#9         # stops the whole flow
/limpar A#9           # shows what it would delete
/limpar A#9 confirmar # really deletes

blocos.rot: flow.json · how the domain declares a gate

abas.html: The phase declares in portao.mostrar what goes to the chat: text goes in the message, audio and images go as files, video goes as a link (a video that is minutes long goes over Telegram's 50 MB limit).

It runs all the way through without stopping for approval, but it still sends to the chat what each gate would have shown. Use it only when you already trust that flow, and never before publishing something you haven't read.

The project documentation records the risk: approving several flows at once without checking can trigger useless waits (the phase that downloads the avatar waits up to 90 minutes before failing when the video was not recorded). Check before you release.

secoes.sub: Use a flow with a gate. If you don't have /promoavatar set up yet, start with | sombra.

exercicios.texto: Run a flow with a gate (like /promoavatar), first with | sombra to see the phases. When it stops, read what arrived in the chat, fix it if needed, and only then send /pronto.
exercicios.pronto: you rejected or corrected at least one text before approving.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Where should the gate of a social media video flow go?
opcoes: Before the first phase, to approve the topic.
After the texts and before the expensive phases and publishing.
perguntas.explica: After what needs your eye, before what costs money or goes out to the world. At the start there is nothing to read; after publishing it's too late.

perguntas.p: The flow stopped at the gate with a wrong text. You send /refazer A#9. What happens?
opcoes: Nothing: /refazer only picks up a phase that failed, and the gate phase is waiting for you.
The text phase is redone with your correction.
perguntas.explica: A phase at the gate did not fail. To change the text, reply to the gate with the correction (when the flow accepts it) or, as a last resort, cancel.

opcoes: Showing the plan (phases, audiences and queues) without queuing anything.
Running the flow without a gate.
perguntas.explica: It's the rehearsal before you spend: you see what would be done. Don't confuse it with | sem-portao, which runs everything without stopping.

perguntas.p: In the simulation, what shows that you are managing, and not just using?
opcoes: Approving fast so the flow keeps moving.
Running with | sem-portao to save time.
Reading the text at the gate, rejecting it with the correction, and only approving the right version.
perguntas.explica: The gate only protects you if you read. Approving without reading let the false promise through; rejecting with a correction reopened the phase and published the right text.
